reconcile.connective: JFB reads the two verses as answering different questions: Adam as federal head of the race in Romans, Eve's deception as the ground for subjection in Timothy.

discrepancy.connective: Ehrman reads the Adam-to-Eve blame shift as a sign 1 Timothy is pseudonymous, reworking Paul to license patriarchal church order.

skeptic.name: Bart D. Ehrman
skeptic.work: Forgery and Counterforgery: The Use of Literary Deceit in Early Christian Polemics
skeptic.attribution: Bart D. Ehrman, Forgery and Counterforgery: The Use of Literary Deceit in Early Christian Polemics (Oxford University Press, 2013), pp. 192-222.

excerpts.excerpt_text: In Rom 5:12, Adam is represented as the first transgressor; but there no reference is made to Eve, and Adam is regarded as the head of the sinning race. Hence, as here, Ti1 2:11, in Gen 3:16, woman's "subjection" is represented as the consequence of her being deceived.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB, commenting on 1 Tim 2:14, explicitly invokes Rom 5:12 to explain the different roles Adam and Eve play in the two texts, resolving the apparent double-blame by distinguishing federal headship (Romans) from the ground of subjection (Timothy).

pd_work.note: JFB is the PD harmonizing voice already surfaced on this row; it directly cross-references Romans 5:12 while explaining 1 Timothy 2:14, which Haley's Alleged Discrepancies does not treat under this specific pairing.
